summary: Revolutionary militia private in Orange County, New York, and probably the brother of Samuel Pringle; John's 5th-great-grand-uncle.
bio:
Benjamin Prindle was born in Connecticut in 1764, probably a son of James Prindle and Hannah (Anar) Turner of Newtown, a brother of David Prindle, born in 1757, and of John's ancestor Samuel Pringle, born in 1767, who named one of his own sons Benjamin.

During the Revolution Benjamin and David Prindle served as privates in the First Regiment of the Orange County militia, earning land bounty rights; the same roll lists several of the Lamoreux men. In 1790 a David Prindle was living at New Cornwall, Orange County, a few households from John Lomereaux and Oliver Davenport, so the Prindles lived among the Lamoreaux family, which helps explain how Samuel Pringle came to marry Martha Lamoreaux. Benjamin died in 1839.

military.note: Benjamin Prindle and David Prindle are listed together under Orange County Militia, First Regiment (land bounty rights) in New York in the Revolution (1898), p.253. The same page lists a John Lamoreux, Isaac Lamore and Nicolas Lamarux. [R4-S1]

researchNotes:
The Prindle Genealogy lists Benjamin Prindle and David Prindle as privates, 1st Regt., Orange Co. Militia (land bounty rights). Round 2 suggested Benjamin as Samuel's father (Samuel named his son Benjamin); Round 3 downgraded this - FamilySearch lists Benjamin (1764) as a son of James Prindle, i.e. Samuel's brother.

In 'New York in the Revolution', Benjamin and David Prindle appear on the same page as the Lamoreux men under the First Regiment of Orange County militia (land bounty rights) ([R4-S1]). In 1790 a David Prindle was living at New Cornwall, Orange Co., a few households from John Lomereaux and Oliver Davenport (see Jean Lamoreaux). So this Prindle family lived among the Lamoreaux family in Orange County, which explains how Samuel Pringle came to marry Martha Lamoreaux. FamilySearch gives Benjamin (b. 1764 in Connecticut, d. 1839) to James Prindle and Hannah (Anar) Turner of Newtown, alongside David (1757) and Samuel (1767), but attaches no sources to Benjamin ([R4-S2]).
